headline: Claude Code Mac Sandbox Fails Open
summary: An analysis of Anthropic's Claude Code macOS sandbox implementation reveals it is disabled by default and fails open, creating unexpected security exposure for developer environments.

slides.title: Is your local AI assistant running completely uncontained?
slides.subtitle: Default configurations can grant broad system access without your active awareness.
slides.body: When powerful AI agents operate locally on your development machine, a missing containment boundary turns minor utility flaws into major system compromises.
slides.deep_dive: Developers frequently trust command-line AI tools with workspace access. If security guardrails are opt-in rather than mandatory, local file systems risk unexpected exposure.
slides.key_fact: Claude Code's sandbox defaults to disabled on macOS environments.
slides.why_it_matters: Unrestricted developer tools expand your local attack surface significantly.

slides.title: The macOS sandbox layer fails open by design
slides.subtitle: Isolation mechanisms rely on external configurations that can easily be bypassed.
slides.body: The security architecture depends on optional flags rather than strict kernel-level enforcement, leaving operating system resources vulnerable if initialization fails.
slides.deep_dive: In modern software defense, a fail-open mechanism means that if the isolation wrapper cannot start, the application proceeds with full privileges instead of halting safely.
slides.key_fact: Sandbox failures drop restrictions instead of blocking execution entirely.
slides.why_it_matters: A safety mechanism that fails open provides a false sense of security.

slides.title: How uncontained execution propagates risk
slides.subtitle: A step-by-step trace of unrestricted local agent access.
slides.body: Understanding how commands flow from an unverified agent to your core operating system files.
slides.deep_dive: Without robust process boundaries, an agent executing terminal commands can interact with sensitive directories far beyond the intended workspace scope.
slides.key_fact: Execution paths bypass isolation when default parameters remain unchanged.
slides.why_it_matters: Chain reactions from local script execution can escalate into system-wide modifications.

steps.title: Default Launch
steps.desc: The application starts without explicit sandboxing flags enabled.

steps.title: Unchecked Boundary
steps.desc: System calls execute with the full privileges of the logged-in user account.

steps.title: Resource Access
steps.desc: Local files and environment variables are exposed to external tool operations.

slides.title: Where the trust boundary breaks down
slides.subtitle: Mapping the direct link between AI tooling and host system files.
slides.body: Visualizing an architecture lacking an enforced security perimeter between terminal agents and host memory.
slides.deep_dive: When security policies are optional, the architectural boundary becomes porous, allowing data to flow freely between untrusted processes and critical directories.
slides.key_fact: Direct host access circumvents standard containerization safeguards.
slides.why_it_matters: Architecture design must treat default states as high-risk environments.

slides.title: Opt-in security versus zero-trust defaults
slides.subtitle: Why relying on developer configuration creates systemic vulnerabilities.
slides.body: Expecting developers to manually enable security wrappers guarantees that many instances will run unprotected.
slides.deep_dive: Secure design patterns mandate that software must fail closed and enforce strict defaults. Making isolation optional shifts the burden incorrectly to end users.
slides.key_fact: Defaults dictate real-world safety more than advanced optional settings.
slides.why_it_matters: Convenience often overrides manual security configuration in fast-paced workflows.

slides.title: Moving from exposed perimeters to defense-in-depth
slides.subtitle: Comparing fragile default states with hardened execution environments.
slides.body: Implementing multiple layers of validation ensures that a single configuration oversight does not compromise your entire workstation.
slides.deep_dive: True defense-in-depth combines strict kernel sandboxing, explicit permission prompts, and least-privilege user accounts to mitigate single points of failure.
slides.key_fact: Layered controls prevent catastrophic failures from single configuration slips.
slides.why_it_matters: Resilient systems anticipate human error and technical failures alike.

slides.title: Actionable steps to secure your AI workflows
slides.subtitle: Verify your local environment settings against common risks today.
slides.body: Apply these essential verification steps to ensure your development machine remains properly isolated.
slides.deep_dive: Regularly auditing local execution privileges and ensuring security flags are explicitly enforced protects your codebase from unexpected agent behaviors.
slides.key_fact: Explicit configuration audits protect against default security oversights.
slides.why_it_matters: Proactive hardening keeps your engineering pipeline secure.
items: Audit current AI tool configuration files for sandbox flags
Verify that security mechanisms fail closed rather than open
Run development agents inside isolated container environments
Limit local user credentials available to assistant processes
